<a id="page-security"></a>

## About this page

When the vault locks, what can see it while it is open, the ways in, and what happens if someone forces you to open it.

#### How it works

Locking closes the vault and forgets its key, so getting back in takes the master password or another way in.

The groups further down change the vault file itself: its passwords, key files and security keys, the duress passwords, and the emergency kit. They are only shown for the vault you opened at the door, not inside a nested or shared one.

#### When to use it

Look here once when you set up, and again whenever your situation changes, such as a new security key or someone you would trust with your vault.

See also [Locking](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-locking), [Duress and decoys](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-duress), [Emergency access](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-emergency-kit), [The vault file](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-vault-file).

<a id="setting-lock-after"></a>

## Lock after no activity

Locks the vault when nobody has used WM Pass for this long.

#### Why it is there

A vault left open on a desk, a shared screen or a borrowed laptop is readable by anyone in front of it. A short timer limits how long that lasts.

#### How it works

Clicking, typing or scrolling in WM Pass counts as use. Using other programs does not, so the timer runs while you work elsewhere.

On the computer the timer runs in the app itself rather than in the window, so it still fires when the window is hidden or minimized and the system has paused it.

#### When to use it

Shorter is safer, and the master password is the price. If you unlock many times a day on a computer only you use, a longer time is reasonable; on a shared or work computer, keep it short.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| 1 minute | Suits a shared computer. You will unlock often. |
| 5 minutes | A fair middle for most people. |
| 15 minutes | Fewer interruptions while you work in the app. |
| 30 minutes | Only where the computer is yours and locks itself. |
| 1 hour | Only where the computer is yours and locks itself. |
| Never | The vault stays open until you lock it, the computer sleeps (if that is on), or WM Pass quits. |

#### Limits

The timer does not protect a vault from a program already running on your computer while it is unlocked.

#### On Android

On the phone it is called Lock after leaving the app.

Locks the vault this long after you leave WM Pass for another app or the home screen.

The timer starts when WM Pass goes into the background and stops when you come back.

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| At once | Locks as soon as you leave the app. |
| 1 min | Time to switch to another app and back without unlocking again. |
| 5 min | Fewer unlocks if you copy several things in a row. |
| 30 min | Only where the phone is yours and locks itself. |
| Never | The vault stays open until you lock it, the screen goes off (if that is on), or the system closes the app. |

See also [Lock when the computer sleeps](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-on-sleep), [Lock when the window is hidden](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-on-hide), [Locking](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-locking).

<a id="setting-lock-on-sleep"></a>

## Lock when the computer sleeps

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

Locks the vault when the computer goes to sleep or its lid is closed.

#### Why it is there

A laptop is most often lost or picked up while it is asleep. With this on, waking it shows the door, not your passwords.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | Waking the computer always means unlocking WM Pass again. |
| Off | The vault can still be open after the computer wakes, until the lock timer runs out. |

See also [Lock after no activity](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-after), [Locking](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-locking).

<a id="setting-lock-screen-off"></a>

## Lock when the screen goes off

*Only in Android.*

Locks the vault when the phone's screen turns off.

#### Why it is there

A phone left on a table or taken from your hand usually has its screen off. With this on, turning it back on shows the door.

See also [Lock after no activity](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-after), [Locking](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-locking).

<a id="setting-lock-on-hide"></a>

## Lock when the window is hidden

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

Locks the vault as soon as its window is minimized, closed to the tray, or covered by another tab.

#### Why it is there

Some people open WM Pass, copy one thing and leave. Locking on hide means the vault is never open when you are not looking at it.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | Every return to the window means unlocking again. Quick search still works only while the vault is open. |
| Off | Hiding the window leaves the vault open until the lock timer runs out. |

#### Limits

With this on, the quick search window and auto-type have nothing to offer once the main window is hidden.

See also [Lock after no activity](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-after), [Keep running in the tray](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-close-to-tray).

<a id="setting-screen-protection"></a>

## Block screenshots

Asks the system to keep WM Pass out of screenshots, screen recordings and screen sharing.

#### Why it is there

A video call or a recording can catch a password you had on show for a second. Other programs that capture the screen see a blank window instead.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | Screenshots and shared screens show WM Pass as blank or black. |
| Off | WM Pass appears in screenshots and shared screens like any other window. Turn it off only while you take a screenshot to show someone. |

#### Limits

macOS and Windows honor it. Linux desktops may ignore it, and a camera pointed at the screen is not stopped by anything.

#### On Android

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | Screenshots show nothing, and the recent apps list shows a blank card. |
| Off | You can take screenshots, and the recent apps list shows what was on screen. |

An accessibility service you have turned on can still read what is on screen.

<a id="setting-clipboard-seconds"></a>

## Clear the clipboard after

Empties the clipboard this long after you copy a password, a code or another secret.

<div class="guide-frame">
<div class="guide-row"><div class="guide-box"><strong>You copy a password</strong></div><span class="guide-side">→</span><div class="guide-box"><svg class="guide-icon" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M200-120q-33 0-56.5-23.5T120-200v-560q0-33 23.5-56.5T200-840h167q11-35 43-57.5t70-22.5q40 0 71.5 22.5T594-840h166q33 0 56.5 23.5T840-760v560q0 33-23.5 56.5T760-120H200Zm0-80h560v-560h-80v120H280v-120h-80v560Zm308.5-571.5Q520-783 520-800t-11.5-28.5Q497-840 480-840t-28.5 11.5Q440-817 440-800t11.5 28.5Q463-760 480-760t28.5-11.5Z"/></svg><strong>Clipboard</strong><span>kept out of its history</span></div><span class="guide-side">→</span><div class="guide-box"><strong>You paste it</strong></div></div>
<div class="guide-down">↓</div>
<div class="guide-row"><div class="guide-box good"><strong>Cleared</strong><span>when the time is up</span></div><div class="guide-box muted"><strong>Left alone</strong><span>if you copied something else</span></div></div>
</div>
<figcaption>A copied secret is cleared after the time you chose, but only if it is still on the clipboard.</figcaption>
</figure>

#### Why it is there

Anything on the clipboard can be pasted by mistake into a chat or a search box, and any program can read it. Clearing it soon after shortens that window.

#### How it works

A copied secret is marked so that clipboard history and clipboard managers that respect the mark leave it out.

When the time is up, WM Pass empties the clipboard only if your secret is still on it. If you have copied something else since, that is left alone.

On Android, a password just made with the generator, its widget or **Set a new password** is not cleared. It is saved nowhere yet and is usually on its way into a sign-up or change-password form, so clearing it there would lose it. It is still marked sensitive, and goes when you copy something else.

The message that says something was copied has a **Clear now** button.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| 15 seconds | Enough to paste once. |
| 30 seconds | Enough to switch windows and paste. |
| 1 minute | For slow forms or a second paste. |
| 2 minutes | For typing into another device by hand. |
| 5 minutes | For a long form, or a password typed in pieces. |
| Never | A copied secret stays until something else replaces it. |

#### Limits

A program reading the clipboard during those seconds still sees the secret. Auto-type and the browser extension fill without the clipboard.

#### On Android

A copied secret is marked as sensitive, so the system's copy preview, and keyboards that respect the mark, do not show it.

When the time is up, WM Pass empties the clipboard if your secret is still on it.

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| 15 s | Enough to paste once. |
| 30 s | Enough to switch apps and paste. |
| 1 min | For slow forms or a second paste. |
| 2 min | For typing into another device by hand. |

An app reading the clipboard during those seconds still sees the secret. Autofill fills without the clipboard.

See also [Auto-type](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-auto-type-enabled), [Copying secrets](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-clipboard).

<a id="action-keyring-unlock"></a>

## Unlock from the system keyring

*Only in the desktop app.*

Keeps this vault's key in the system keyring, so the door can open it without the master password.

#### How it works

The key is wrapped and stored with the operating system's secret store, for this vault file only. Turning it off removes it from the keyring.

#### When to use it

On a computer only you use, where typing the master password many times a day is the bigger risk.

#### Limits

A convenience, not protection: any program running in your session can ask the keyring for the key.

macOS builds have no Secure Enclave unlock, because the app is not signed.

See also [Locking](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-locking), [The master password](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-master-password).

<a id="action-passkey-unlock"></a>

## Unlock with a passkey

*Only in the browser extension.*

Opens this vault with Touch ID, Windows Hello or your phone, in place of the master password.

#### How it works

WM Pass makes a passkey for itself on this device. What the passkey answers seals the vault's key inside WM Pass's own engine, and only that sealed copy is kept in the browser. Turning it off throws the copy away.

#### When to use it

On a computer only you use, where typing the master password many times a day is the bigger risk.

#### Limits

The sealed copy opens nothing without the passkey, so a copied browser profile does not open the vault.

The passkey belongs to wmpass.pages.dev, and your browser or phone may keep it with your other passkeys. Deleting it there turns this off.

A browser without passkeys that can give an app a secret (the PRF extension) does not offer this.

See also [Unlock from the system keyring](/guide/settings/security/#action-keyring-unlock), [Locking](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-locking), [The master password](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-master-password).

<a id="action-change-password"></a>

## Change it

Changes the master password and keeps the vault's key as it is.

#### How it works

The vault is protected by a random key. Your password only unlocks that key, so changing it rewraps the key and leaves your items untouched. It is quick.

#### When to use it

When you want a stronger password, or think someone may have seen yours but has not had a copy of the file.

#### Limits

Backups and copies made before the change still open with the old password. If someone may have a copy of the file, use [Change it and rekey](/guide/settings/security/#action-rekey) instead.

See also [Change it and rekey](/guide/settings/security/#action-rekey), [The master password](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-master-password), [The vault file](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-vault-file).

<a id="action-rekey"></a>

## Change it and rekey

Changes the master password and gives the vault a new key, so old copies of the file cannot follow new changes.

#### Why it is there

If someone has an older copy of your vault and its password, a plain password change does not shut them out of what you add later. A new key does.

#### How it works

Everything in the vault is encrypted again under the new key. Every other way in is dropped and the new password becomes the only one.

#### When to use it

When a copy of the file and its password may both be in someone else's hands, such as a lost laptop that was unlocked, or a trustee you no longer trust.

#### Limits

Other passwords, key files and security keys stop working until you add them back under [Unlock methods](/guide/settings/security/#group-security-methods).

An emergency kit made before the rekey stops working. Make a new one.

An old copy of the file can still be read by whoever has it and its old password. Rekeying protects what comes after.

See also [Change it](/guide/settings/security/#action-change-password), [Emergency kit](/guide/settings/security/#action-emergency-kit), [The vault file](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-vault-file).

## Unlock methods

#### How it works

The vault file has a fixed number of slots. Each way in fills one, and the empty ones are random bytes, so nobody can tell from the file how many ways in there are, or whether one of them is a duress password.

Click a password in the list to remove it. A vault always keeps at least one way in.

See also [Add a password](/guide/settings/security/#action-add-password), [Add a key file](/guide/settings/security/#action-add-key-file), [Add a security key](/guide/settings/security/#action-add-security-key), [Duress and decoys](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-duress).

<a id="action-add-password"></a>

## Add a password

Adds a second password that opens the same vault.

#### When to use it

A long password for everyday use and a longer one written down and kept somewhere safe.

A password for a partner, with its own name, that you can remove later without changing yours.

#### Limits

Anyone with any of these passwords and the file can read the whole vault.

See also [Unlock methods](/guide/settings/security/#group-security-methods), [Duress and decoys](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-duress).

<a id="action-add-key-file"></a>

## Add a key file

Adds a way in that needs both a password and a file you choose.

#### Why it is there

A stolen password alone is no longer enough. Someone would also need the file, which you can keep on a USB stick or another device.

#### How it works

Choose any file that will not change, such as a photo you will keep. Its contents are read, never stored in the vault. From then on the door asks for the file as well as the password.

#### Limits

Lose the file and this way in is gone. Keep another way in, or a copy of the file somewhere safe. Editing the file, even resaving a photo, breaks it.

See also [Unlock methods](/guide/settings/security/#group-security-methods), [Add a security key](/guide/settings/security/#action-add-security-key).

<a id="action-add-security-key"></a>

## Add a security key

Adds a way in that needs a YubiKey or another FIDO2 key plugged in and touched.

#### Why it is there

A security key cannot be copied. Someone who learns your password still cannot open the vault without the key in their hand.

#### How it works

The key computes a secret from a value stored in the vault. That secret joins your password in unlocking the vault key. See [Hardware key](/guide/settings/hardware/) for the setup.

#### Limits

Lose the key and this way in is gone. Register a second key, or keep another way in.

See also [Hardware key](/guide/settings/hardware/), [Unlock methods](/guide/settings/security/#group-security-methods).

<a id="action-wipe-password"></a>

## Wipe password

A second password that erases the vault on this device when someone types it at the door. It looks exactly like a wrong password.

<div class="guide-frame">

<div class="guide-down">↓</div>
<div class="guide-row"><div class="guide-box good"><strong>Your password</strong><span>opens your vault</span></div><div class="guide-box"><strong>Decoy password</strong><span>opens the decoy</span></div><div class="guide-box warn"><strong>Lockout password</strong><span>refuses all for an hour</span></div><div class="guide-box danger"><strong>Wipe password</strong><span>erases this copy</span></div></div>
</div>
<figcaption>Every password looks the same at the door. What happens depends on which one is typed.</figcaption>
</figure>

#### When to use it

If you might be made to unlock your device by someone you cannot refuse, and you have backups somewhere they cannot reach.

#### Limits

It erases only this device's copy. Backups, synced copies and other devices are not touched, which is how you get the vault back.

Disks may keep traces after an erase. This resists a quick look, not a forensic examination.

See also [Duress and decoys](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-duress), [Lockout password](/guide/settings/security/#action-lockout-password), [Decoy vault](/guide/settings/security/#action-decoy-vault).

<a id="action-lockout-password"></a>

#### When to use it

When you want a way to stall without losing anything: nothing is erased, and after the hour the vault opens normally.

See also [Duress and decoys](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-duress), [Lock and refuse passwords now](/guide/settings/security/#action-panic-now).

<a id="action-decoy-vault"></a>

## Decoy vault

A separate vault, opened by its own password at the same door. Fill it with a few believable logins.

<figure class="guide-figure">
<div class="guide-frame">
<div class="guide-row"><div class="guide-box"><svg class="guide-icon" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 -960 960 960" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M240-80q-33 0-56.5-23.5T160-160v-400q0-33 23.5-56.5T240-640h40v-80q0-83 58.5-141.5T480-920q83 0 141.5 58.5T680-720v80h40q33 0 56.5 23.5T800-560v400q0 33-23.5 56.5T720-80H240Zm0-80h480v-400H240v400Zm296.5-143.5Q560-327 560-360t-23.5-56.5Q513-440 480-440t-56.5 23.5Q400-393 400-360t23.5 56.5Q447-280 480-280t56.5-23.5ZM360-640h240v-80q0-50-35-85t-85-35q-50 0-85 35t-35 85v80ZM240-160v-400 400Z"/></svg><strong>The door</strong></div></div>
<div class="guide-down">↓</div>
<div class="guide-row"><div class="guide-box good"><strong>Your password</strong><span>opens your vault</span></div><div class="guide-box"><strong>Decoy password</strong><span>opens the decoy</span></div><div class="guide-box warn"><strong>Lockout password</strong><span>refuses all for an hour</span></div><div class="guide-box danger"><strong>Wipe password</strong><span>erases this copy</span></div></div>
</div>
<figcaption>Every password looks the same at the door. What happens depends on which one is typed.</figcaption>
</figure>

#### How it works

The door looks the same whichever password you type, and nothing in the file says the decoy exists. Each password opens its own vault.

#### Limits

It resists a quick look under pressure. It does not stand up to forensics, or to someone who has an older copy of your files to compare.

See also [Duress and decoys](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-duress), [Wipe password](/guide/settings/security/#action-wipe-password).

<a id="action-panic-now"></a>

## Lock and refuse passwords now

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

Locks the vault at once and refuses every password for an hour.

#### When to use it

When you are about to hand your device over and want it to stay shut for a while. Nothing is lost.

See also [Lockout password](/guide/settings/security/#action-lockout-password), [Duress and decoys](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-duress).

<a id="action-emergency-kit"></a>

## Emergency kit

Splits a recovery key into shares for people you trust, so that enough of them together can open your vault if you cannot.

<figcaption>Here, any two of three. Fewer shares than that number reveal nothing at all.</figcaption>

#### Why it is there

Nothing can recover a forgotten master password, and nobody can open your vault if something happens to you. A kit gives a few people that power together, and none of them alone.

#### How it works

Choose how many people, and how many of them it takes, such as any three of five. Each person gets one share.

Fewer than that number learn nothing at all from their shares. Enough of them, with a copy of the vault file, can set a new password and open it.

Save the file, print it, give each person their share, then delete the file.

#### Limits

They can do it at once. Any waiting period is a promise between you, not something software can enforce.

Rekeying the vault stops the shares working. Make a new kit afterwards.

See also [Emergency access](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-emergency-kit), [Change it and rekey](/guide/settings/security/#action-rekey).

<a id="setting-network-allowed"></a>

## Allow network features

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension and Android.*

The one switch every feature that talks to the internet needs. Off means nothing leaves this device.

#### Why it is there

WM Pass works fully without a network. Some extras cannot: checking breaches, making aliases, syncing with a server, signing in to an account, and checking for updates. Each one says what it sends, and to whom, on its own page.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Off | No feature can reach the internet. Pages that need it say so and offer to turn this on. |
| On | Network features run when you use them. Nothing is sent in the background except what you set up, such as scheduled backups or update checks. |

#### Limits

Syncing with other devices on your own network uses its own pairing, under Settings, Sync and accounts.

See also [Breaches](/guide/settings/breaches/), [Email aliases](/guide/settings/aliases/), [Sync and accounts](/guide/settings/sync/), [Updates](/guide/settings/updates/).

<a id="action-fingerprint-unlock"></a>

## Unlock with fingerprint

*Only in Android.*

Opens the vault with your fingerprint, or another biometric the phone rates as strong, in place of the master password.

#### Why it is there

A long master password is slow to type on a phone many times a day.

#### How it works

Turning it on asks for your fingerprint once. The vault's key is then encrypted under a key in the phone's secure hardware, in StrongBox where the phone has it, and that key works only after a fingerprint check. An app that skips the prompt gets nothing it can use.

The door asks for your fingerprint as soon as it opens. If you close the prompt, **Use fingerprint** brings it back, and **Use password** goes to the password field.

Adding a new fingerprint to the phone makes the system destroy that key. This turns itself off, and the master password opens the vault next time.

#### When to use it

On a phone only you use, where a fingerprint is quicker than a long password.

#### Limits

It does not protect against someone who can make you touch the sensor. Duress passwords work only when typed, so they do nothing here.

It lives on this phone only. A backup, or the vault on another device, still needs the master password.

See also [Lock after no activity](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-after), [Locking](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-locking), [The master password](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-master-password), [Wipe password](/guide/settings/security/#action-wipe-password).

<a id="group-security-autofill"></a>

## Autofill and panic

*Only in Android.*

How other apps and your watch reach the vault, and what a panic app can make WM Pass do.

#### How it works

Autofill, WM Keyboard and the watch get nothing while the vault is locked. Autofill can ask for your fingerprint over the app you are in, or bring up the door; the keyboard and the watch cannot.

A panic app can lock or wipe the vault at any time.

See also [Autofill service](/guide/settings/security/#action-autofill-service), [Let WM Keyboard fill](/guide/settings/security/#setting-keyboard-access), [Show on my watch](/guide/settings/security/#setting-wear-access), [When a panic app signals](/guide/settings/security/#setting-panic-action).

<a id="setting-autofill-inline"></a>

## Inline suggestions

*Only in Android.*

Shows matching logins in the keyboard's suggestion row, where the keyboard supports it, in place of a list under the field.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | With a keyboard that supports it, logins appear as chips above the keys. With other keyboards they appear in a list under the field. |
| Off | Suggestions appear only in the list under the field. |

#### Limits

Android 11 and later only.

A chip shows the login's name and username, never its password. Tapping it goes through WM Pass, as tapping a row in the list does.

See also [Autofill service](/guide/settings/security/#action-autofill-service), [Offer to save passwords](/guide/settings/security/#setting-autofill-save), [Filling logins](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-autofill).

<a id="setting-autofill-save"></a>

## Offer to save passwords

*Only in Android.*

After you sign in somewhere with a password WM Pass does not have, asks whether to save it.

#### How it works

When a login form is sent, WM Pass looks for logins that match the app or site and the username. If one already has that password, nothing is asked.

Otherwise it asks. With no match, **Save** makes a new login named after the site or the app. With a match, a button for each matching login puts the new password on it, and **Save as a new login** keeps both. **Not now** saves nothing.

A login saved from an app remembers the app's package name and signing certificate, so it is offered there next time.

#### Limits

It works only while WM Pass is this phone's autofill service.

See also [Autofill service](/guide/settings/security/#action-autofill-service), [Inline suggestions](/guide/settings/security/#setting-autofill-inline), [Filling logins](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-autofill).

<a id="setting-keyboard-access"></a>

## Let WM Keyboard fill

*Only in Android.*

Lets the WM Pass tool in WM Keyboard browse your vault, type from it, add logins to it and change passwords in it, while the vault is open.

#### How it works

The keyboard can only ask. It cannot open the vault, and gets an answer only while the vault is open here.

It is shown every item that is not in the trash or on the hidden shelf, those saved for the app in front first: each one's name, the line under it, and whether it has a password or a code. Its search goes through the vault's own search.

Opening an item there shows its fields. A plain field, such as a username or a website, is shown as it is; a secret is only named. A secret is sent only when you tap to type that one field.

Copying a field from the keyboard is done here: WM Pass puts it on the clipboard itself, marked sensitive and cleared after the time set under [Clear the clipboard after](/guide/settings/security/#setting-clipboard-seconds), so a copied secret never passes through the keyboard.

The keyboard can add a login, with a name, username, password and website, and change an item's password. The old password stays in the item's history. A login added from an app is tied to that app by its signing certificate, so it comes first there next time, unless the app is a browser.

Its **New password** makes one with the generator as you set it up here.

Its code chip offers the current one-time code for the app in front, matched by that app's package name and signing certificate.

Each app checks the other's signing certificate on every call, so another app using WM Keyboard's name is refused.

It turns on by itself the first time WM Keyboard is installed. Once you set it either way, your choice stands.

#### Limits

A password typed this way passes through the keyboard's process, as anything you type does, and so does one you type into the keyboard's own form to save here. To keep passwords out of there, use the [autofill service](/guide/settings/security/#action-autofill-service) instead.

The keyboard types and copies nothing into a field that asks it not to learn, such as a private browser tab.

See also [Autofill service](/guide/settings/security/#action-autofill-service), [Inline suggestions](/guide/settings/security/#setting-autofill-inline), [Buttons on WM Keyboard's strip](/guide/settings/security/#feature-keyboard-chips).

<a id="feature-keyboard-chips"></a>

## Buttons on WM Keyboard's strip

*Only in Android.*

While you type in some of WM Pass's own fields with WM Keyboard, the keyboard offers the buttons next to that field as chips above its keys.

#### How it works

In a card's number, it offers **Scan the card**. In the name on the card and the expiry date it does too, when the card scanner is Google's, since only that one reads them.

In a Wi-Fi network's name and password, it offers **Fill in from a QR code** and **Pick a network saved on this phone**.

A tap on a chip does exactly what the button on the screen does.

Each screen gets a fresh name for its fields, and the keyboard sends that name back with the tap. A tap meant for a screen that has closed does nothing.

#### Limits

The fields tell the keyboard only which buttons they have, never what they hold. WM Pass takes a tap only from the real WM Keyboard, checked by its signing certificate, and the keyboard reads the fields only of the real WM Pass.

It does not need [Let WM Keyboard fill](/guide/settings/security/#setting-keyboard-access): a chip only presses a button here, and nothing from the vault goes to the keyboard.

See also [Let WM Keyboard fill](/guide/settings/security/#setting-keyboard-access), [Reader](/guide/settings/editor/#setting-card-reader).

<a id="setting-wear-access"></a>

## Show on my watch

*Only in Android.*

Lets the WM Pass app on your paired Wear OS watch show one-time codes and favorite logins, while the vault on this phone is open.

#### How it works

The watch keeps nothing. It asks the phone each time, and the phone answers only while this is on and the vault is open. If the phone is locked or out of reach, the watch says so.

Each answer carries the current codes for up to 20 items, with favorite and pinned items first, and the names and usernames of up to 20 favorite or pinned logins. A password is sent only when you tap a favorite, and the watch shows it for 20 seconds.

A tile on the watch shows your first code. The complication opens the app and shows no code.

It turns on by itself the first time a paired watch with WM Pass asks. Turn it off and it stays off.

#### Limits

Codes and tapped passwords reach the watch through Google's Wearable API, which answers only the same app, signed the same way, on a watch paired with this phone.

Anyone wearing or holding the watch can see your codes while the vault on the phone is open.

The F-Droid and offline builds have no such row, because they leave out Google's Wearable API.

<a id="action-autofill-service"></a>

## Autofill service

*Only in Android.*

Opens Android's prompt to make WM Pass this phone's autofill service, so it can fill logins in other apps and in browsers.

#### How it works

Tap a username or password field in another app and WM Pass offers up to six matching logins, and **Search WM Pass** for any other. While the vault is locked it offers **Unlock WM Pass** instead.

With fingerprint unlock set up, tapping **Unlock WM Pass** brings up only the fingerprint prompt, over the app you are in. **Use password** opens the door instead. The same goes for a passkey, and the fingerprint that opened the vault also approves the sign-in.

Nothing leaves the vault until you tap a suggestion. WM Pass then fills the username, the password and a one-time code if the screen has a box for it. A time-based code with no box on the screen is copied to the clipboard, for a site that asks on the next one.

Apps are matched by package name and signing certificate, not by name. Sites are matched by web address.

#### Limits

Only a browser WM Pass knows can vouch for the web address it shows. When any other app reports one, such as a page inside its own window, WM Pass names that app and asks **Fill it** or **Do not fill**.

See also [Inline suggestions](/guide/settings/security/#setting-autofill-inline), [Offer to save passwords](/guide/settings/security/#setting-autofill-save), [Filling logins](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-autofill), [Passkeys](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-passkeys), [Let WM Keyboard fill](/guide/settings/security/#setting-keyboard-access), [Browsers](/guide/settings/security/#action-browser-autofill).

<a id="action-browser-autofill"></a>

## Browsers

*Only in Android.*

Says whether Chrome, and each browser built on it, hands its pages to your autofill service, and opens that browser's setting when it does not.

#### How it works

Since Chrome 135, Chrome fills from its own password manager unless you turn on **Autofill using another service** in Chrome's settings, under Autofill services. Until then WM Pass never hears about a page in Chrome, so it cannot offer anything there.

Each browser built on Chrome, such as Brave, Edge, Vivaldi or Samsung Internet, has its own copy of the setting. Each one on this phone that says which way it is set gets a row here; tapping it opens that browser's page for the setting.

Once WM Pass is your autofill service, the vault list also asks once about a browser that is still on its own password manager.

#### Limits

A browser that does not answer is left out: it is older than the setting, or was built without it. Firefox and the browsers built on it use your autofill service already and need nothing.

See also [Autofill service](/guide/settings/security/#action-autofill-service), [Filling logins](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-autofill).

<a id="setting-panic-action"></a>

## When a panic app signals

*Only in Android.*

What WM Pass does when a panic app, such as Ripple, sends its signal. Until you choose, signals are ignored.

#### How it works

Choosing **Lock** or **Wipe** shows [Panic apps](/guide/settings/security/#setting-panic-app) below it, where you pick the apps to listen to. Signals from any other app are ignored, so no app can keep the vault locked or erase it. With **Lock** and no app chosen, any app may ask for a lock. A wipe always needs a chosen app.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| None | Panic signals do nothing. |
| Lock | A signal locks the vault and refuses every password for an hour. Nothing is lost. |
| Wipe | A signal from an app you chose erases the vault on this phone with no warning. |

#### Limits

If a signal does not say which app sent it, WM Pass cannot tell it came from an app you chose, so it never wipes for it.

A wipe erases this phone's vault, its attachments and its fingerprint unlock, and forgets its backup places and sync accounts, so their addresses are not left behind. Backups, synced copies and other devices are not touched, which is how you get the vault back.

Flash storage may keep traces after an erase.

See also [Panic apps](/guide/settings/security/#setting-panic-app), [Panic lock tile](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-panic-tile), [Wipe password](/guide/settings/security/#action-wipe-password), [Lockout password](/guide/settings/security/#action-lockout-password), [Duress and decoys](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-duress).

<a id="setting-panic-app"></a>

## Panic apps

*Only in Android.*

The apps whose panic signal WM Pass listens to, picked from the apps on this phone.

#### How it works

Apps known to send the signal, Ripple and Panic Button, are listed first. Tick the ones you use and tap **Done**, or **Wipe on their signal** when the choice above is Wipe.

#### Limits

WM Pass compares each app with the one Android says sent the signal. Choose for a wipe only an app you trust to erase your vault.

See also [When a panic app signals](/guide/settings/security/#setting-panic-action).

<a id="setting-widget-access"></a>

## Show on widgets

*Only in Android and the desktop app.*

Lets the Codes and Favorites widgets show one-time codes and the names of favorites, while the vault is open.

#### How it works

Off, those two widgets say only that they are turned off. With the vault locked, they say only that it is locked, and name nothing.

Locking, from anywhere, empties them at once.

No other widget shows anything from inside the vault, whether this is on or not.

#### Limits

Anyone who can see your screen can see these codes and names while the vault is open.

#### On Android

Off, those two widgets say only that they are turned off. With the vault locked, they say only that it is locked, and name nothing.

Locking, from anywhere, empties them at once. If Android ends WM Pass while they show something, they are drawn locked again within a few minutes.

No other widget shows anything from inside the vault, whether this is on or not.

See also [Widgets](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-home-widget), [Codes on widgets](/guide/settings/widgets/#setting-widget-codes).
